newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Census forms to be shortest in 180 years.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Census forms to be shortest in 180 years.

text.p: The U.S. Census Bureau has joined the downsizing trend and announced on Monday it hopes to have the shortest questionnaire in 180 years for the once-a-decade count in year 2000.

The Bureau said it submitted to Congress for review a short form of seven topics covering name, age, sex, relationship to others in the residence, marital status, possible Hispanic origin and whether a home is owned or rented.
A longer questionnaire covering 34 questions will be sent to people in one out of every six houses.
Census officials said the short form was the most concise since 1820. In the 1990 census the short form covered 12 subjects and the long form covered 38.
